title: Worktree-redirected repo-owned writes are invisible to the daemon between a restart and the branch merge
wanted_capability: Repo-owned artifacts redirected into a worktree checkout (gap notes via write_dir, knowledge entries via the Knowledge write-redirect map, thread records via record_dir) should remain queryable across a daemon restart that happens before the worktree branch merges into the base. Today the redirect state is deliberately transient (serde-skip / in-memory side map, cleared on reload) and reload only spools repo-owned files from registered base roots — so a restart in the redirect window makes the entry/gap vanish from list/render/inject surfaces until the branch lands in the base checkout. Self-heals on merge, but the window is silent: nothing tells the operator that N redirected records are currently carried only by un-merged worktree branches. Wanted: either (a) central-store retention for redirected records until their committed file is observed under a base root (the load-side id-collision self-heal already supports dropping them later), or (b) a doctor/inbox surface that enumerates redirected records living only in worktree checkouts.
missing_primitive: central-store retention (or visibility surface) for repo-owned records whose committed file is redirected into an un-merged worktree
fallback_used: Mirrored the existing gaps-store contract knowingly when adding the knowledge write redirect (commit 372fac2): accept the window, rely on prompt fold-to-base (the corpus-worktree-scoping flow folded within the same session, closing the window in minutes).
evidence: crates/bbox-knowledge/src/knowledge.rs (write_redirects map: cleared in reload; central_snapshot excludes repo-owned carriers)
